name: WhatFontIs-Bench
description: WhatFontIs-Bench is a synthetic test set for font family identification: a single word, set in a known font, printed or painted on real surfaces and in real scenes, with the exact font, the text and the position of every letter recorded for each image. Made by WhatFontIs, the font finder that identifies fonts from images. v1.0: 600 fonts (200 sans-serif, 200 serif, 100 slab serif, 100 monospaced), 11,995 JPEG images (20 per font), three image types (texture, scene, object) and three difficulty levels (easy, medium, hard). One word per image, 7-12 letters, taken from COCO-Text v2. Annotations: per-image labels (labels.jsonl) and COCO format (annotations.json) with word and letter positions. Font files are not included. Baseline: the WhatFontIs API (searching its whole catalogue of over 1.2 million fonts) finds the right font family at rank 1 for 83.7 % of the images, in the top 5 for 93.3 % and in the top 20 for 96.5 % (September 2026). Unzip the four image archives into v1/ (they create v1/scenes/NNNNN.jpg); see README.md for all details. Official page: https://www.whatfontis.com/WhatFontIs-Bench.html Credits: backgrounds are CC0 1.0 (Poly Haven, ambientCG, Wikimedia Commons via Openverse; per-file details in backgrounds.json). Words from COCO-Text v2 (CC BY 4.0). The typefaces belong to their designers and foundries.
